items.d: **Target**: all landholding farmer families. **Design**: ₹6,000 a year in three instalments, DBT to the Aadhaar-seeded account, with land-record and e-KYC verification. **Numbers**: about **9.8 crore beneficiaries** and over **₹3.7 lakh crore** disbursed since 2019 — the largest income-support programme in the world by beneficiary count. **Gap**: tenant farmers and landless cultivators are excluded because the trigger is land title.

items.t: PMFBY — Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
items.d: Premium capped at **2% (kharif), 1.5% (rabi) and 5% (commercial/horticultural)** with the balance shared by the Centre and state; **voluntary since 2020**. Around 4 crore farmer applications annually; claims paid over ₹1.7 lakh crore against premiums of about ₹35,000 crore paid by farmers. Uses **YES-TECH and WINDS** for yield estimation and weather data, cutting the crop-cutting-experiment delay. Several states exited over the state-share burden.

**Electronic National Agriculture Market** — 1,400+ mandis across 23 states integrated, 1.8 crore farmers and 2.5 lakh traders registered, with assaying, e-payment and inter-mandi trade. The binding constraint is that **APMC is a state subject**: e-NAM cannot create a single national market by itself, which is what the repealed 2020 farm laws attempted.

**₹1 lakh crore** of medium-to-long term debt financing for post-harvest infrastructure — with a **3% interest subvention and credit guarantee up to ₹2 crore**; over ₹50,000 crore sanctioned across 1 lakh+ projects. Complements the **10,000 FPO scheme (₹6,865 crore)** and the world's largest **decentralised grain storage plan** in the cooperative sector.

**National Mission on Natural Farming (₹2,481 crore)** targeting 1 crore farmers and 7.5 lakh ha in 15,000 clusters, with Bhartiya Prakritik Kheti Bio-input Resource Centres. Andhra Pradesh's **Community-Managed Natural Farming** is the flagship state model, and Sikkim is the **world's first fully organic state (2016)**. Counterpoint for balance: Sri Lanka's abrupt 2021 organic switch and the resulting yield collapse.

Announced in Budget 2025-26 — convergence of **36 existing schemes across 11 ministries** in **100 low-productivity districts**, covering 1.7 crore farmers, on the Aspirational Districts template: measure, rank, converge. The agricultural counterpart of the ADP.

**MGNREGA** — ~₹86,000 crore a year, 5-6 crore households employed, average days worked per household ~50 against the 100 guaranteed; being restructured as **VB-G RAM G**. **PMGSY** — 7.6 lakh km of rural roads connecting 99%+ of eligible habitations; **DAY-NRLM** for SHGs; **SVAMITVA** for property cards.

**14 sectors, ₹1.97 lakh crore**: mobiles and electronics, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, automobiles, ACC batteries, textiles, food processing, white goods, solar modules, drones, telecom, speciality steel. Design: incentive on **incremental** sales over a base year, paid only on achieved investment and production — output-linked, not input-subsidy. Mobile manufacturing is the success case; some sectors have underperformed on disbursal.

The **investment-and-turnover definition** (revised upward in Budget 2025-26: micro ₹2.5 cr/₹10 cr, small ₹25 cr/₹100 cr, medium ₹125 cr/₹500 cr) removed the disincentive to grow. **CGTMSE** guarantee cover expanded to ₹10 crore; **TReDS** for receivables discounting; the **45-day payment rule** under Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act; **PM Vishwakarma (₹13,000 crore)** for 18 traditional trades; **PM SVANidhi** for street vendors.

**ELI scheme (₹99,446 crore)** from Budget 2024-25, targeting **3.5 crore jobs over two years** through three parts: **Scheme A** — one month's EPF wage (up to ₹15,000) to first-timers; **Scheme B** — support to employers and employees in manufacturing; **Scheme C** — reimbursement of employers' EPFO contribution up to ₹3,000 a month. The first large-scale Indian attempt at a **wage-subsidy approach to formalisation**.

**Four codes consolidating 29 laws** — **Code on Wages (2019)** with a statutory national floor wage and universal minimum wage; **Industrial Relations Code (2020)** raising the retrenchment threshold to **300 workers** and requiring 60-day strike notice; **Social Security Code (2020)** extending cover to **gig and platform workers** with an aggregator contribution of 1-2% of turnover; **OSH Code (2020)**. Notified but implementation awaited pending state rules — the largest pending labour reform.

**Startup India** — tax holiday for three years under 80-IAC, **Fund of Funds ₹10,000 crore** through SIDBI, **Startup India Seed Fund ₹945 crore**, self-certification and faster exit. **Atal Innovation Mission** — 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs and Atal Incubation Centres. **1.6 lakh+ recognised startups, 100+ unicorns, 3rd largest ecosystem**, with ~45% from tier-2/3 cities.

items.t: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
items.d: **₹75,021 crore** to install rooftop solar on **1 crore households**, with up to **300 units of free electricity a month**, a central subsidy of up to ₹78,000, collateral-free loans at ~7%, and a model solar village per district. The largest domestic rooftop programme in the world by target.

**₹19,744 crore** — target **5 MMT of annual green hydrogen production by 2030** with 125 GW of associated renewable capacity, ₹8 lakh crore of investment and 6 lakh jobs; **SIGHT** programme incentivises electrolyser manufacturing and hydrogen production. India aims to be a **global hub for production and export**, with green ammonia for fertiliser and shipping as the near-term markets.

The **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023**, framed under the **Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022** — a **compliance mechanism** with intensity targets for obligated entities from 2026, plus an offset mechanism for non-obligated entities, administered by BEE with the Grid Controller as registry. Succeeds the **PAT (Perform, Achieve and Trade)** scheme and the REC market.

**Lifestyle for Environment** — launched at COP26 and carried into the **G20 New Delhi Declaration**, shifting from 'mindless consumption' to 'mindful utilisation'; the demand-side complement to supply-side decarbonisation. **Circular economy**: EPR regimes for plastic, e-waste, battery and tyre waste; **Vehicle Scrappage Policy**; the ban on identified single-use plastics (2022); and **GOBARdhan** for waste-to-energy.

**Jal Jeevan Mission** — rural tap connections from **3.23 crore (17%) in 2019 to over 15 crore (~80%)**. **Atal Bhujal Yojana** — ₹6,000 crore in 7 states with community water security plans as the condition for incentives. **Namami Gange (₹20,000 crore+)** and the **Arth Ganga** livelihood model. **Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain**; and the **National River Linking Project**, whose first link is **Ken-Betwa (₹44,605 crore)**.

**DM Act, 2005** with NDMA (PM-chaired), SDMA, DDMA, NDRF (16 battalions) and NIDM. The **DM (Amendment) Act, 2025** gives statutory status to the **National Crisis Management Committee and the High Level Committee**, empowers NDMA to prepare the national plan itself and create an **Urban Disaster Management Authority** for state capitals and large cities. Funds: **NDRF/SDRF plus dedicated mitigation funds (NDMF/SDMF)** on the 15th FC's recommendation.

**NQM — ₹6,003 crore (2023-31)**: intermediate-scale quantum computers of 50-1,000 physical qubits, satellite-based secure quantum communication over 2,000 km, and four thematic hubs. **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (₹50,000 crore, of which ₹36,000 crore is to come from private and philanthropic sources)** — created by the ANRF Act, 2023, replacing SERB, with the PM as ex-officio President.

**UPI** (18-19 bn transactions/month, ~half of global real-time payments), **Aadhaar Enabled Payment System**, **Account Aggregator** framework for consent-based data sharing, **ONDC** to unbundle e-commerce, **OCEN** for cash-flow-based lending, **e-RUPI** vouchers, and the **e-Rupee CBDC** pilots in retail and wholesale. Together these are what India exports as **Digital Public Infrastructure**.

**I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre)** with the **National Cybercrime Reporting Portal** (22+ lakh complaints a year), the **Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System** and its 1930 helpline, **CERT-In** as the nodal agency under the IT Act (with the 2022 directions on 6-hour incident reporting), **NCIIPC** for critical information infrastructure, and the **National Cyber Security Policy 2013** — long overdue for replacement.

**PMLA, 2002** — ED as the investigating agency, with the **twin conditions for bail under Section 45** upheld in *Vijay Madanlal Choudhary* (2022); **FIU-IND** for financial intelligence. India's **FATF Mutual Evaluation (2024)** placed it in the **'regular follow-up' category — the highest tier, achieved by only a handful of countries** — while flagging delays in prosecution and the need to supervise non-financial sectors.

**NIA** under the NIA Act, 2008 (post-26/11), with extraterritorial jurisdiction after the 2019 amendment; **NATGRID** linking 11 agencies to 21 databases; **MAC (Multi Agency Centre)** for intelligence sharing; **CCTNS** and the **Interoperable Criminal Justice System**; **NSG, CAPFs (~10 lakh personnel)**, and the **Chief of Defence Staff and Department of Military Affairs (2019)** with theatre commands under consideration. **Agnipath (2022)** for military recruitment.
